prompts.pear: Use case: scientific-educational. Original premium realistic botanical illustration of FOUR immature green Asian pear fruit shape examples in a clean two-by-two grid on warm ivory, with wide blank gutters and no panel frames. No text, no labels, no numbers, no arrows, no cut marks, no watermark. Each young pear has delicate green skin with fine natural lenticels, a small calyx at its upper distal end, and a slender green stalk extending downward from its lower end; depict fruit in early developing upward orientation, not ripe bottle-shaped European pears. Distinct shape examples: TOP LEFT a balanced smooth vertically oval immature pear, broadly rounded sides and a subtly flattened calyx-end shoulder; TOP RIGHT an immature fruit broadly swollen across its upper calyx half and narrowing markedly toward the bottom stalk, fig-like overall outline; BOTTOM LEFT a visibly asymmetric misshapen immature pear with one side irregularly bulging inward/outward compared with the other; BOTTOM RIGHT an otherwise oval immature pear with several visible longitudinal grooves or furrows running along its side. All four are separate individual fruit, fully visible, same modest scale and similar green maturity; no overlaid artificial symbols. High-quality dimensional painterly botanical realism, real textured fruit bodies and subtle shadows, not flat polygons or circles. Treat these as general qualitative visual examples only, not a diagnostic reference, cultivar identification, universal thinning decision or measured exact contour. Independent composition and independently painted specimens, no copied source art. Ensure the four requested qualitative distinctions remain readable.
prompts.satsuma: Use case: scientific-educational. Original premium realistic botanical instructional painting showing SIX separate observation examples of immature green satsuma mandarin citrus fruit and small branch sections, arranged in a clear two-column by three-row grid on warm ivory with generous blank gutters. No frames, no text, no numbers, no arrows, no crosses, no symbols, no tools or hands. Preserve fixed reading order. TOP LEFT: a green fruit hanging from a short twig with very few leaves, just one small leaf nearby, so sparse foliage is visible. TOP RIGHT: two hanging green fruit pressed against and partly overlapping one another on a short leafy branch. MIDDLE LEFT: a single green fruit with an obviously discolored yellow-brown patch on its peel, attached to a little leafy twig, no insects or mold. MIDDLE RIGHT: a small clearly misshapen asymmetric green fruit attached to a short leafy twig; convey abnormal outline, not measured size. BOTTOM LEFT: a green fruit growing UPWARD above a horizontal twig on an upward-pointing fruit stalk, with natural calyx at base near stalk; this must visibly contrast with the downward-hanging fruit in other examples. BOTTOM RIGHT: a hanging green fruit with a visible superficial tan scrape/scar on peel, attached to short leafy twig. All subjects fully visible, recognizable citrus leaves with believable veins, green dimpled fruit surfaces, realistic stalk attachments, detailed painterly botanical realism, not flat icons/circles/polygons. These are qualitative observation examples associated with source teaching, NOT pest diagnosis, fruit grading or a universal instruction to remove every illustrated fruit. No quantitative prescription, no numbered counts, no yield or quality guarantee. Independent composition and art, not copied source illustration.
